rationale: This is a cosmetic re-parameterization of the archived "R&D Sell-Through Spread"/"R&D Product-Launch Sell-Through" (same sell-through × R&D-intensity interaction, only a lag, at- vs sale-scaling, and a positive-only truncation differ), and the truncation makes the short leg an arbitrary tie-broken subset of the large mass of zeros rather than an economically identified group.

Mechanically identical to the archived "R&D Liquidity-Coverage Spread" (R&D intensity × net short-term-debt-minus-cash), with only denominator rescaling and a one-year lag, so it is a variant of an already-strong result rather than a substantively different hypothesis.

This is the third pass at the same post-acquisition R&D-cut mechanism already tested in both MIN ("Post-Acquisition R&D Crowding Out") and signed-product ("Acquisition Renewal Spread") form, differing only by zero-truncation, which additionally leaves the long leg populated by an undifferentiated mass of zero-valued firms.

The goodwill × signed sell-through pairing is a genuinely new combination in this archive and offers an interpretable purchased-versus-organic-intangible contrast, though the sell-through leg is close to a rescaled sales-growth-minus-inventory-growth (accruals/inventory-growth) construct and the goodwill weight will be near zero for most firms.

Substituting gross profit per employee for sales per employee is more than a rescaling — it merges the margin and labor-scalability channels tested separately in the archive and is internally consistent with the positive expected sign — but it remains an incremental fusion of two prior signals and inherits their moderate portfolio evidence.

Direct variant of the archived "R&D-Enhanced Fixed-Capital Productivity" (same gross-PPE turnover growth × R&D intensity), with only a MIN-to-product change, lag, and positive-only gate, and the gate again collapses the short leg into ranked ties at zero.
